reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) concerns different alloy systems (Al0.3CoCrFeNi and CoCrFeMnNi) and does not provide specific support for a twinning-dominated transition in Co-free FeNiCrMn. E1 reports twinning as one contributor in Al0.3CoCrFeNi but does not establish a rate threshold or dominance; E2 mentions serrations in CoCrFeMnNi but attributes them to dynamic strain aging, not a twinning transition. The key premises about FeNiCrMn are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: A critical strain rate (~10^3 s⁻¹) exists above which mechanical twinning becomes dominant in FeNiCrMn
This twinning transition markedly enhances strain hardening and maintains ductility
The transition is driven by dislocation inability to accommodate strain solely via slip at high rates
The mechanism is expected in as-cast, coarse-grained FCC FeNiCrMn at 295–350 K
